headline: Youth found dead on stairs of relative's house in Raozan
summary: The 36-year-old man had arrived late at night to visit family, but no one opened the door for him.
details: Police recovered the body of Muhammad Rashed, 36, from the stairs of a relative's house in the Southpara village of Raozan, Chattogram.
Rashed, a resident of Fatikchhari, had left home on Monday afternoon to visit his maternal grandfather's house in Saudagarpara.
According to police and local sources, Rashed arrived at his relative's home around midnight on Monday night.
Because it was late, the occupants of the house—two women—did not recognize his voice and did not open the door.
Local residents discovered his body on the stairs the following morning with severe injuries to his head.
The body has been sent to the hospital morgue for an autopsy to determine the exact cause of death.
Local police from the Neoyapara police outpost have launched an investigation into the incident.
caption:
He arrived at his relative's house at midnight, but no one opened the door. By morning, he was found dead on the stairs.

Police recovered the body of Muhammad Rashed, 36, from the stairs of a relative's house in the Southpara village of Raozan, Chattogram.

Rashed, a resident of Fatikchhari, had left home on Monday afternoon to visit his maternal grandfather's house in Saudagarpara.

According to police and local sources, Rashed arrived at his relative's home around midnight on Monday night.

Because it was late, the occupants of the house—two women—did not recognize his voice and did not open the door.

Local residents discovered his body on the stairs the following morning with severe injuries to his head.

The body has been sent to the hospital morgue for an autopsy to determine the exact cause of death.

Local police from the Neoyapara police outpost have launched an investigation into the incident.

headline_marked: 2 police officers [[injured in mugger attack]] in Dhaka's Adabor
headline: 2 police officers injured in mugger attack in Dhaka's Adabor
summary: The Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Adabor Police Station and a Sub-Inspector were attacked with sharp weapons during a raid in Mohammadpur.
details: Two police officers, including the Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Adabor Police Station, were injured after being attacked with sharp weapons by muggers during a drive in Dhaka’s Mohammadpur area this afternoon.
The injured officers are OC Jahidul Islam and Sub-Inspector Tarun of the same police station, according to Assistant Commissioner (AC) Abdullah Al Mamun of the Mohammadpur Zone.
The police drive was launched around 4:00 pm in the Beribadh area to arrest suspects involved in a morning mugging incident where a bKash agent shop owner was beaten and robbed of his mobile phone.
Upon sensing the police presence, the suspects allegedly attacked the officers with sharp weapons, leading to the injuries.
Police opened fire in self-defence during the attack, leaving two suspected muggers, identified as Rasel (26) and Amir (25), injured.
The two injured suspects were taken to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital for treatment.
Police have arrested four alleged muggers in connection with the incidents, and drives are continuing to apprehend the remaining suspects.
